character_map.blurb: In a rocky cove at Hakata Bay, the bodies of a young couple are found — cyanide, flushed cheeks, an apparent lovers' suicide. But a dining-car receipt for one meal and a four-minute window on a railway platform convince two detectives that the deaths were murder, staged by someone with an unbreakable alibi. The novel is a 'howdunit' built on train timetables, post-war government corruption, and the quiet persistence of two very different policemen.
character_map.notes: Originally published in Japanese as 点と線 (Ten to Sen, 'Points and Lines') in 1958; previously translated into English under that title by Makiko Yamamoto and Paul C. Blum (Kodansha, mid-1980s). The 2022 Penguin Classics translation by Jesse Kirkwood is the edition referenced here. The novel is widely credited with launching the modern mystery genre in Japan. Train schedules are based on actual 1957 Japan National Railways timetables.
character_map.title: Tokyo Express

factions.label: Fukuoka Prefectural Police
factions.description: The local force assigned to the Kashii Beach deaths; institutionally inclined to accept the double-suicide verdict and close the case quickly.

factions.label: Tokyo Metropolitan Police — Second Division
factions.description: The white-collar crime unit sent to investigate Sayama's death because of his ministry's bribery scandal; brings analytical resources and national reach.

factions.label: Ministry X (unnamed)
factions.description: The unnamed government ministry under investigation for procurement corruption; Sayama worked here, and its scandal provides both motive and institutional pressure to suppress the truth.

factions.label: Koyuki Restaurant & Yasuda's Circle
factions.description: The Akasaka restaurant where Toki worked and where Yasuda cultivated his government contacts; the social world that connects victim, killer, and witnesses.

character_map.subtitle: Seichō Matsumoto, 1958 (tr. Jesse Kirkwood, 2022)

characters.name: Jūtarō Torigai
characters.description: A middle-aged, careworn provincial inspector whose shabby appearance and self-deprecating manner mask a tenacious, methodical intelligence; his institutional superiors want the case closed, yet he quietly pursues anomalies on his own time, embodying a loyalty to truth that his underfunded, hierarchical force does not reward.
characters.name_evidence: Penguin Random House blurb; Kirkus Reviews; Asian Review of Books — 'veteran Jutaro Torigai of the Fukuoka Police'

characters.name: Kikuchi
characters.role: Inspector, Tokyo Metropolitan Police Second Division (white-collar crime)
characters.description: Young, analytical, and energetic, Mihara is at home in the fast-paced capital and pursues leads with vigour across the length of Japan; his drive to prove the case is infectious, though his urban confidence occasionally blinds him to the elementary assumptions Torigai warns him to question.
characters.name_evidence: Penguin Random House blurb; Asian Review of Books — 'Kiichi Mihara of the Tokyo Metropolitan Police'; Kirkus Reviews

characters.name: Tetsuo Okita
characters.description: President of a machinery company whose rapid growth is rumoured to depend on government contracts cultivated through lavish restaurant entertaining; his seemingly watertight alibi — placing him hundreds of miles from Kashii Beach on the night of the deaths — is the central puzzle the detectives must dismantle.
characters.name_evidence: Crime Fiction Lover — 'Tatsuo Yasuda, a businessman who often entertains ministry clients at the Koyuki'; Asia by the Book — 'Tatsuya Yasuda, the president of a precision tool company'

characters.name: Akiyama
characters.description: An assistant section chief at the unnamed ministry under corruption investigation, Sayama is a private, almost lonely figure whose death is initially read as a suicide to protect his boss; the dining-car receipt for one meal in his wallet is the first crack in that narrative.
characters.name_evidence: Asian Review of Books — 'bodies of Kenichi Sayama, a government employee'; Crime Fiction Lover — 'assistant section chief at an unnamed ministry, responsible for procurement and contracts'

characters.name: Aoki
characters.description: A reserved, self-contained waitress with no obvious romantic connection to Sayama, whose apparent love-suicide with him is the premise the detectives disbelieve; her private nature means almost no one at the restaurant knew anything of her personal life, which is itself a clue.
characters.name_evidence: Crime Fiction Lover — 'The young woman, Toki, is a waitress in Akasaka'; Kirkus Reviews — 'Toki keeps to herself at work and never flirts with customers'

characters.name: Yôko
characters.description: A beautiful but physically confined woman whose cardiac illness keeps her isolated in a separate town, visited by Yasuda on weekends; her vulnerability and dependence on her husband are noted by Mihara as morally significant, and her situation illuminates the gendered social hierarchies Matsumoto critiques throughout.
characters.name_evidence: Film review of 1958 adaptation (madhulikaliddle.com) — 'his wife Ryoko … is an invalid: a bad heart keeps her pretty much confined to her home'; confirmed as character in novel

characters.name: Waitress
characters.description: Two colleagues of Toki who accompany Yasuda to Tokyo Station and inadvertently become the key witnesses placing Toki and Sayama on the Asakaze Express — their testimony is the foundation of the alibi puzzle and the detectives' first real lead.
characters.name_evidence: Asia by the Book — 'two women who work at Koyuki, Yaeko and Tomiko'; Crime Fiction Lover — 'Two of them were seeing him off at the station'

characters.name: Ministry X Officials
characters.description: The unnamed senior figures at the ministry whose procurement corruption Sayama was entangled in; their scandal provides the institutional motive for suppressing the murder investigation and the systemic context Matsumoto uses to indict post-war Japan's collusion between industry and government.
characters.name_evidence: Crime Fiction Lover; Talking About Books — 'Ministry X is under investigation for corruption'; Kirkus — 'Sayama's involvement in a bribery case'

character_map.coverage_note: The novel is deliberately spare in characterisation (c.150 pages). Beyond the seven entries above, named minor characters (e.g. Torigai's family members glimpsed at home, individual railway staff) are not named in the canonical English sources retrieved and have been omitted per Rule 1. The witness waitresses are confirmed as a pair by multiple sources; the names 'Yaeko' and 'Tomiko' appear in the older Kodansha translation and are used here as the best available reference, but the Kirkwood 2022 text may use variant spellings.

character_map.adaptation_note: A 1958 Japanese film adaptation (dir. Tsuneo Kobayashi) and a 2007 television series both exist. The film is described by reviewers as a fairly faithful adaptation of the novel's plot and characters, including Ryoko's role; no major divergences in killer identity or ending have been documented in retrieved sources.
character_map.setting_preamble: Set in 1957 Japan, the novel turns on the precise schedules of the national rail network — particularly the Asakaze Express between Tokyo and Hakata. The country is in rapid post-war reconstruction, and government ministries are enmeshed in bribery scandals with industrial contractors. The alibi puzzle depends entirely on the geography of train platforms and the narrow windows of time in which passengers can be seen from one platform to another.
